prompt:
Product owner's brief for PR-1 (Customer onboarding and identity checks (KYC)):
New customers register with their full name, e-mail, national identity number and date of birth. Customers must be at least 18. A compliance officer reviews each registration and verifies or rejects it; nobody can verify themselves. A customer who is not verified cannot open an account. National id and date of birth are personal data and must never appear in events, logs or messages.


Public contract the team agreed:
namespace Bank.Modules.Customers.Domain:
  enum KycStatus { Pending, Verified, Rejected }
  sealed class Customer { string Id (the user id, primary key); string FullName; string Email; [Pii] string NationalId;
                          [Pii] DateOnly DateOfBirth; KycStatus Status { get; private set; } (starts Pending); string? DecidedBy;
                          DateTimeOffset RegisteredAt;
                          void Verify(string officerId); void Reject(string officerId) }   // only from Pending, else InvalidOperationException
  sealed record CustomerRegistered(string CustomerId, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
  sealed record CustomerVerified(string CustomerId, string VerifiedBy, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
  sealed record CustomerRejected(string CustomerId, string RejectedBy, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
namespace Bank.Modules.Customers.Application:
  sealed record RegisterCustomerRequest(string FullName, string Email, string NationalId, DateOnly DateOfBirth)
  interface ICustomerService {
    Task<Customer> RegisterAsync(RegisterCustomerRequest request, CancellationToken ct = default);  // for the signed-in user;
        // already registered -> InvalidOperationException; under 18 on IClock's date -> ArgumentException; empty fields -> ArgumentException
    Task<Customer> VerifyAsync(string customerId, CancellationToken ct = default);   // compliance officer only, never themselves -> UnauthorizedAccessException; unknown -> KeyNotFoundException
    Task<Customer> RejectAsync(string customerId, CancellationToken ct = default);   // same rules as VerifyAsync
    Task<Customer?> GetAsync(string customerId, CancellationToken ct = default); }
  sealed class CustomerService(BankDbContext db, ICurrentUser user, IClock clock, IEventBus bus) : ICustomerService
  sealed class KycAccountOpeningRule(BankDbContext db) : IAccountOpeningRule   // not Verified (or unknown) -> UnauthorizedAccessException
CustomersModule registers ICustomerService and KycAccountOpeningRule as IAccountOpeningRule.
BankDbContext gets: DbSet<Customer> Customers
HTTP: POST api/customers (register yourself), GET api/customers/me, POST api/customers/{id}/verify, POST api/customers/{id}/reject (Compliance policy)


Bank coding conventions:
# Coding conventions for Nordbank (the Builder must follow these)

Stack: C# / ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 8+), EF Core (SQLite), xUnit. No new NuGet packages.

## Layout — one folder per module, one folder per layer
src/Bank.Api/Modules/<Module>/
  Api/          controllers + DTOs            (HTTP layer)
  Application/  services + interfaces         (use cases)
  Domain/       entities, enums, events       (business rules)
  Data/         repositories (optional)       (database access)
  <Module>Module.cs   static class with AddXModule(this IServiceCollection): services.AddScoped<IThing, Thing>()
Register a new module in Program.cs above the "// MODULES:" line.
Add a new table as a DbSet in src/Bank.Api/Data/BankDbContext.cs above the "// TABLES:" line.
Each module already has a CONSTITUTION.md written by the humans who own it: follow its rules.

## Rules
- Namespaces follow folders: Bank.Modules.<Module>.<Layer>.
- Controllers: [ApiController], [Route("api/...")], and ALWAYS an [Authorize(Policy = Policies.X)] (Bank.Modules.Auth.Policies:
  Customer, Staff, LoanOfficer, Compliance, Admin). Roles are in Bank.Modules.Auth.Roles.
- Current user: inject Bank.Modules.Auth.Application.ICurrentUser (UserId, IsInRole). Never trust user ids from request bodies.
- Time: inject Bank.Shared.Time.IClock and use clock.UtcNow. Never call DateTime.Now / DateTimeOffset.UtcNow directly.
- Settings: inject Bank.Shared.Settings.BankSettings (DefaultCurrency, SupportedCurrencies, DailyTransferLimit).
- Money: decimal only. Round to cents with Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero).
- Money moves ONLY through Bank.Modules.Ledger.Application.ILedger.PostTransferAsync(from, to, amount, reference),
  which returns the transfer id and works in ONE currency. The bank's own accounts:
  Bank.Modules.Ledger.Domain.BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.X, currency) with kinds
  LoanFunding, FeeIncome, FxClearing, DepositHolding, InterestExpense, Suspense (EUR, SEK, USD).
- Accounts: Bank.Modules.Accounts.Application.IAccountService (GetAsync, IsOwnerAsync, ForOwnerAsync). Never edit Account.Balance.
- State machines: an entity owns its status (private setter) and changes it only through methods that check the current state.
- Entities: public parameterless constructor and public settable properties (except a status with a private setter),
  so the database and tests can create them.
- Events: sealed records implementing Bank.Shared.Events.IDomainEvent (with DateTimeOffset OccurredAt), published with
  IEventBus.PublishAsync(...). Handlers implement IEventHandler<TEvent> and are registered in their module.
- Personal data properties get [Pii] (Bank.Shared). Never put personal data in events, logs or messages.
- Do not name a type "Ledger" outside the Ledger module (namespace clash).
- Keep files small; one public type per file unless they are tiny records.

prompt:
Product owner's brief for PR-2 (Payments between accounts):
A customer can send money from one of their own accounts to any other account in the bank. Every payment request carries an idempotency key chosen by the app; if the same customer sends the same key again (for example after a timeout), the bank returns the first payment and does not move money again. Customers can send at most the daily transfer limit from BankSettings per calendar day (UTC). Amounts must be positive whole cents. In this PR both accounts must have the same currency.


Public contract the team agreed:
namespace Bank.Modules.Payments.Domain:
  enum PaymentStatus { Completed, Held, Rejected }
  sealed class Payment { Guid Id; string IdempotencyKey; string CustomerId; Guid FromAccountId; Guid ToAccountId;
                         decimal Amount; string Currency; PaymentStatus Status; Guid? TransferId; string? Reference; DateTimeOffset CreatedAt }
  sealed record PaymentCompleted(Guid PaymentId, string CustomerId, decimal Amount, string Currency, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
namespace Bank.Modules.Payments.Application:
  sealed record PaymentRequest(string IdempotencyKey, Guid FromAccountId, Guid ToAccountId, decimal Amount, string? Reference)
  sealed class DailyLimitExceededException : InvalidOperationException
  interface IPaymentService {
    Task<Payment> PayAsync(PaymentRequest request, CancellationToken ct = default);
        // from-account not owned by the caller -> UnauthorizedAccessException; amount <= 0 or not whole cents -> ArgumentException;
        // same caller + same key -> the existing payment, no new money movement; over the daily limit -> DailyLimitExceededException;
        // insufficient funds -> InsufficientFundsException (from the Ledger); different currencies -> CurrencyMismatchException
    Task<IReadOnlyList<Payment>> ForCustomerAsync(string customerId, CancellationToken ct = default); }
  sealed class PaymentService(BankDbContext db, ILedger ledger, IAccountService accounts, ICurrentUser user, IClock clock,
                              BankSettings settings, IEventBus bus) : IPaymentService
BankDbContext gets: DbSet<Payment> Payments
HTTP: POST api/payments, GET api/payments (Customer policy)

  "title": "PR-2: Intra-bank customer payments between accounts with idempotency and UTC daily limit",
  "user_story": "As an authenticated bank customer, I want to transfer a positive whole-cent amount in the same currency from one of my own accounts to any other account in the bank using an idempotency key, so that I can safely send money without duplicate transfers on retries or exceeding my daily transfer limit.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Authentication and authorization: Both POST api/payments and GET api/payments require [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)], derive the caller exclusively from ICurrentUser.UserId (ignoring any user ID in request data), and GET api/payments returns only payments belonging to the authenticated customer via IPaymentService.ForCustomerAsync.",
    "Source account ownership: If FromAccountId does not exist or is not owned by the current user (checked via IAccountService), PayAsync throws UnauthorizedAccessException and does not move funds or persist a completed payment.",
    "Amount and precision validation: PaymentRequest.Amount must be strictly greater than 0 and have at most two decimal places (whole cents, verified against Math.Round(amount, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero) == amount); invalid amounts throw ArgumentException before calling the ledger.",
    "Same-currency enforcement: Both FromAccountId and ToAccountId must share the same currency; if their currencies differ, PayAsync throws CurrencyMismatchException without calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync.",
    "Idempotency: PaymentRequest.IdempotencyKey is required (empty or whitespace keys throw ArgumentException) and scoped to (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) with a unique database constraint on BankDbContext.Payments; if the same customer submits a request with an existing IdempotencyKey, PayAsync returns the stored Payment without calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync or publishing PaymentCompleted again.",
    "Daily transfer limit: Before posting to the ledger, PayAsync sums the customer's completed payments for the current UTC calendar day (using IClock.UtcNow.UtcDateTime.Date, never DateTime.Now or DateTimeOffset.UtcNow directly); if existing daily total plus request.Amount exceeds BankSettings.DailyTransferLimit, PayAsync throws DailyLimitExceededException.",
    "Money movement and ledger errors: Funds are moved exclusively through ILedger.PostTransferAsync(fromAccountId, toAccountId, amount, reference), storing the returned TransferId on Payment; insufficient balance propagates InsufficientFundsException from the ledger and does not create a Completed payment.",
    "Payment entity state and eventing: Payment owns its Status (private setter, using PaymentStatus { Completed, Held, Rejected }), records CreatedAt from IClock.UtcNow, persists via BankDbContext.Payments, and upon completion publishes PaymentCompleted(PaymentId, CustomerId, Amount, Currency, OccurredAt) through IEventBus without including PII such as Reference in events or logs.",
    "Module wiring: PaymentsModule registers IPaymentService and related services in Program.cs above // MODULES:, and BankDbContext exposes DbSet<Payment> Payments above // TABLES:, adhering to the Bank.Modules.Payments.{Api,Application,Domain} namespace layout."
  ],
  "out_of_scope": [
    "Cross-currency payments or foreign exchange conversion via FxClearing.",
    "External or interbank transfers (such as SEPA, SWIFT, ACH, or external beneficiary management).",
    "Scheduled, future-dated, or recurring payments and standing orders.",
    "Compliance hold, fraud review, or manual approval/rejection workflows beyond including Held and Rejected in the PaymentStatus enum.",
    "Payment cancellation, reversal, chargebacks, or refunds after completion.",
    "Transfer fees, commissions, or fee postings to FeeIncome.",
    "Staff, LoanOfficer, Compliance, or Admin endpoints to view or manage other customers' payments.",
    "Per-account or per-currency custom transfer limits overriding BankSettings.DailyTransferLimit."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "Race condition on concurrent retries with the same IdempotencyKey could double-charge the customer if not enforced by a database unique index on (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) and atomic transaction handling.",
    "Race condition on concurrent payments from the same customer could allow total daily transfers to bypass BankSettings.DailyTransferLimit if the daily total check and payment persistence are not serialized or isolated.",
    "Fractional-cent rounding bugs or floating-point arithmetic could create or destroy money; all amounts must remain decimal and reject non-whole-cent inputs rather than silently rounding.",
    "Scoping idempotency keys globally instead of per CustomerId would allow one customer to probe or receive another customer's Payment record.",
    "Missing ownership validation on FromAccountId or trusting a client-supplied CustomerId would allow unauthorized transfers out of another customer's account.",

    "Leaking Reference or customer personal data into logs, exception messages, or PaymentCompleted events would violate bank PII rules."
  ]

Product owner's brief for PR-3 (Currency exchange and cross-currency payments):
The bank holds EUR, SEK and USD. Add exchange rates: 1 EUR = 11.50 SEK and 1 EUR = 1.08 USD; other pairs go through EUR (SEK to USD = from SEK to EUR, then EUR to USD). Converted amounts are rounded to cents, half away from zero. Payments may now go between accounts in different currencies: the payer is debited in their currency, the payee is credited the converted amount, and the money passes through the bank's FxClearing account of each currency. The daily transfer limit now counts every payment in its EUR equivalent.


Public contract the team agreed:
namespace Bank.Modules.Fx.Application:
  interface IFxService {
    decimal Rate(string fromCurrency, string toCurrency);                 // same currency -> 1; unknown currency -> ArgumentException
    decimal Convert(decimal amount, string fromCurrency, string toCurrency); }   // rounded to cents, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero
  sealed class FxService : IFxService     // no constructor arguments
Payment gets: decimal CreditedAmount; string CreditedCurrency; decimal Rate   (same currency: CreditedAmount = Amount, Rate = 1)
PaymentService gets IFxService as a constructor argument (after BankSettings): cross-currency payments no longer throw CurrencyMismatchException.

Product owner's brief for PR-12 (Hold large payments to new payees for review):
To fight fraud, a payment of 5,000 EUR or more (EUR equivalent) to an account the customer has never paid before is held: the money (amount + fee) leaves the payer's account and waits in the bank's Suspense account, the payment status is Held, and the customer is told it is being checked. A compliance officer then releases it (the payee is credited) or rejects it (the payer gets everything back). Officers cannot decide on their own payments.

  sealed record PaymentRejected(Guid PaymentId, string RejectedBy, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent

    Task<IReadOnlyList<Payment>> HeldAsync(CancellationToken ct = default);
    Task<Payment> ReleaseAsync(Guid paymentId, CancellationToken ct = default);   // compliance officer only; own payment -> UnauthorizedAccessException; not Held -> InvalidOperationException
    Task<Payment> RejectAsync(Guid paymentId, string reason, CancellationToken ct = default); }
  sealed class PaymentReviewService(BankDbContext db, ILedger ledger, ICurrentUser user, IClock clock, IEventBus bus, INotifier notifier) : IPaymentReviewService

# Coding conventions for Nordbank (the Builder must follow these)

Stack: C# / ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 8+), EF Core (SQLite), xUnit. No new NuGet packages.

## Layout — one folder per module, one folder per layer
src/Bank.Api/Modules/<Module>/
  Api/          controllers + DTOs            (HTTP layer)
  Application/  services + interfaces         (use cases)
  Domain/       entities, enums, events       (business rules)
  Data/         repositories (optional)       (database access)
  <Module>Module.cs   static class with AddXModule(this IServiceCollection): services.AddScoped<IThing, Thing>()
Register a new module in Program.cs above the "// MODULES:" line.
Add a new table as a DbSet in src/Bank.Api/Data/BankDbContext.cs above the "// TABLES:" line.
Each module already has a CONSTITUTION.md written by the humans who own it: follow its rules.

## Rules
- Namespaces follow folders: Bank.Modules.<Module>.<Layer>.
- Controllers: [ApiController], [Route("api/...")], and ALWAYS an [Authorize(Policy = Policies.X)] (Bank.Modules.Auth.Policies:
  Customer, Staff, LoanOfficer, Compliance, Admin). Roles are in Bank.Modules.Auth.Roles.
- Current user: inject Bank.Modules.Auth.Application.ICurrentUser (UserId, IsInRole). Never trust user ids from request bodies.

- Settings: inject Bank.Shared.Settings.BankSettings (DefaultCurrency, SupportedCurrencies, DailyTransferLimit).
- Money: decimal only. Round to cents with Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero).
- Money moves ONLY through Bank.Modules.Ledger.Application.ILedger.PostTransferAsync(from, to, amount, reference),
  which returns the transfer id and works in ONE currency. The bank's own accounts:
  Bank.Modules.Ledger.Domain.BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.X, currency) with kinds
  LoanFunding, FeeIncome, FxClearing, DepositHolding, InterestExpense, Suspense (EUR, SEK, USD).
- Accounts: Bank.Modules.Accounts.Application.IAccountService (GetAsync, IsOwnerAsync, ForOwnerAsync). Never edit Account.Balance.
- State machines: an entity owns its status (private setter) and changes it only through methods that check the current state.
- Entities: public parameterless constructor and public settable properties (except a status with a private setter),
  so the database and tests can create them.
- Events: sealed records implementing Bank.Shared.Events.IDomainEvent (with DateTimeOffset OccurredAt), published with

- Do not name a type "Ledger" outside the Ledger module (namespace clash).

**Purpose:** The only place money moves: double-entry postings in one currency.
**Owner:** Finance · **Risk:** HIGH

REQUIREMENT:
# PR-2: PR-2: Intra-bank customer payments between accounts with idempotency and UTC daily limit

**Story.** As an authenticated bank customer, I want to transfer a positive whole-cent amount in the same currency from one of my own accounts to any other account in the bank using an idempotency key, so that I can safely send money without duplicate transfers on retries or exceeding my daily transfer limit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Authentication and authorization: Both POST api/payments and GET api/payments require [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)], derive the caller exclusively from ICurrentUser.UserId (ignoring any user ID in request data), and GET api/payments returns only payments belonging to the authenticated customer via IPaymentService.ForCustomerAsync.
- [ ] Source account ownership: If FromAccountId does not exist or is not owned by the current user (checked via IAccountService), PayAsync throws UnauthorizedAccessException and does not move funds or persist a completed payment.
- [ ] Amount and precision validation: PaymentRequest.Amount must be strictly greater than 0 and have at most two decimal places (whole cents, verified against Math.Round(amount, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero) == amount); invalid amounts throw ArgumentException before calling the ledger.
- [ ] Same-currency enforcement: Both FromAccountId and ToAccountId must share the same currency; if their currencies differ, PayAsync throws CurrencyMismatchException without calling ILedger.Pos

ITEMS:
0. [critical] Missing unique constraint on (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) in BankDbContext
   facts: The index configured for Payment on (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) does not call .IsUnique(). Without a unique database constraint, duplicate retries with the same CustomerId and IdempotencyKey succeed on SaveChangesAsync instead of triggering DbUpdateException, allowing duplicate payments, duplicate ledger transfers, and duplicate PaymentCompleted events.
1. [critical] PayAsync checks daily limit and calls ledger before looking up existing idempotency key

- Migrating or converting existing customer accounts from EUR or other currencies to SEK.

# Coding conventions for Nordbank (the Builder must follow these)

Stack: C# / ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 8+), EF Core (SQLite), xUnit. No new NuGet packages.

## Layout — one folder per module, one folder per layer
src/Bank.Api/Modules/<Module>/
  Api/          controllers + DTOs            (HTTP layer)
  Application/  services + interfaces         (use cases)
  Domain/       entities, enums, events       (business rules)
  Data/         repositories (optional)       (database access)
  <Module>Module.cs   static class with AddXModule(this IServiceCollection): services.AddScoped<IThing, Thing>()
Register a new module in Program.cs above the "// MODULES:" line.
Add a new table as a DbSet in src/Bank.Api/Data/BankDbContext.cs above the "// TABLES:" line.
Each module already has a CONSTITUTION.md written by the humans who own it: follow its rules.

## Rules
- Namespaces follow folders: Bank.Modules.<Module>.<Layer>.
- Controllers: [ApiController], [Route("api/...")], and ALWAYS an [Authorize(Policy = Policies.X)] (Bank.Modules.Auth.Policies:
  Customer, Staff, LoanOfficer, Compliance, Admin). Roles are in Bank.Modules.Auth.Roles.
- Current user: inject Bank.Modules.Auth.Application.ICurrentUser (UserId, IsInRole). Never trust user ids from request bodies.
- Time: inject Bank.Shared.Time.IClock and use clock.UtcNow. Never call DateTime.Now / DateTimeOffset.UtcNow directly.
- Settings: inject Bank.Shared.Settings.BankSettings (DefaultCurrency, SupportedCurrencies, DailyTransferLimit).
- Money: decimal only. Round to cents with Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero).
- Money moves ONLY through Bank.Modules.Ledger.Application.ILedger.PostTransferAsync(from, to, amount, reference),
  which returns the transfer id and works in ONE currency. The bank's own accounts:
  Bank.Modules.Ledger.Domain.BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.X, currency) with kinds
  LoanFunding, FeeIncome, FxClearing, DepositHolding, InterestExpense, Suspense (EUR, SEK, USD).
- Accounts: Bank.Modules.Accounts.Application.IAccountService (GetAsync, IsOwnerAsync, ForOwnerAsync). Never edit Account.Balance.
- State machines: an entity owns its status (private setter) and changes it only through methods that check the current state.
- Entities: public parameterless constructor and public settable properties (except a status with a private setter),
  so the database and tests can create them.
- Events: sealed records implementing Bank.Shared.Events.IDomainEvent (with DateTimeOffset OccurredAt), published with
  IEventBus.PublishAsync(...). Handlers implement IEventHandler<TEvent> and are registered in their module.
- Personal data properties get [Pii] (Bank.Shared). Never put personal data in events, logs or messages.
- Do not name a type "Ledger" outside the Ledger module (namespace clash).
- Keep files small; one public type per file unless they are tiny records.

PR PR-1: Customer onboarding and identity checks (KYC)
REQUIREMENT:
# PR-1: PR-1: Customer onboarding and identity checks (KYC)

**Story.** As a new customer, I want to register my personal identity details for compliance review so that once verified I am eligible to open a bank account, while ensuring underage or unverified applicants are blocked.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Domain types exist in Bank.Modules.Customers.Domain: enum KycStatus { Pending, Verified, Rejected }, sealed class Customer (with parameterless constructor, Id, FullName, Email, [Pii] NationalId, [Pii] DateOfBirth, Status with private setter defaulting to Pending, DecidedBy, RegisteredAt, Verify(string officerId), Reject(string officerId)), and sealed record IDomainEvent types CustomerRegistered(string CustomerId, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt), CustomerVerified(string CustomerId, string VerifiedBy, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt), and CustomerRejected(string CustomerId, string RejectedBy, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt).
- [ ] Customer.Verify(officerId) and Customer.Reject(officerId) transition Status from Pending to Verified or Rejected respectively and set DecidedBy to officerId; invoking either method when Status is not Pending throws InvalidOperationException.
- [ ] ICustomerService.RegisterAsync registers a Customer for the signed-in user (Id = ICurrentUser.UserId) with Status = KycStatus.Pending and RegisteredAt = IClock.UtcNow, persists it to BankDbContext.Customers, and publishes CustomerRegistered via IEventBus.
- [ ] ICustomerService.RegisterAsync throws ArgumentException 

ITEMS:

# PR-9: PR-9: Update BankSettings for Swedish launch (SEK default currency and 5,000 EUR daily transfer limit)

**Story.** As the bank preparing for the Swedish launch and complying with regulatory guidance, I want Bank.Shared.Settings.BankSettings updated so that new accounts default to SEK and the daily transfer limit is reduced from 10,000 to 5,000 EUR equivalent for all customers, with no other behavioral changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Bank.Shared.Settings.BankSettings has DefaultCurrency set to "SEK" (changed from "EUR").
- [ ] Bank.Shared.Settings.BankSettings has DailyTransferLimit set to 5_000m (decimal 5000.00, changed from 10_000m).
- [ ] Bank.Shared.Settings.BankSettings SupportedCurrencies remains unchanged (EUR, SEK, USD).
- [ ] When an authenticated Customer (or authorized Staff/Admin role per existing account creation policy) creates a new account without specifying a currency, the created account uses DefaultCurrency ("SEK").
- [ ] When an authenticated Customer (or authorized role) creates a new account explicitly specifying another supported currency (such as "EUR" or "USD"), the account is still created in that requested supported currency.
- [ ] Existing accounts retain their previously assigned currencies and balances; only newly created accounts without an explicit currency default to "SEK".
- [ ] For any Customer initiating transfers, the cumulative daily transfer limit check enforces 5_000m EUR equivalent (using decimal arithmetic and Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero) where EUR equivalent conversion applies): a transfer causing the daily total to equal 5,000.00 EUR equivalent succeeds, while a transfer causing the daily total to exceed 5,000.00 EUR equivalent (e.g., 5,000.01 EUR equivalent or a second transfer pushing the UTC day total above 5,000.00) is rejected with the existing daily limit validation error and posts no ledger movement.
- [ ] Authorization policies, roles, current user identity resolution via ICurrentUser, and UTC day boundary calculation via IClock remain unchanged; no customer or role can bypass the 5,000m daily transfer limit unless already permitted by existing policy.
- [ ] All existing modules and tests that depend on BankSettings continue to pass after updating any test assertions that previously assumed EUR default or 10,000m limit.

## Out of scope
- Converting or migrating existing customer accounts from EUR or USD to SEK.
- Adding new currencies or removing existing currencies from SupportedCurrencies.
- Introducing per-customer, tiered, or role-specific daily transfer limits.
- Adding an API endpoint or UI to edit BankSettings at runtime.
- Modifying FX conversion rates, fee schedules, interest rates, or loan rules.
- Changing account creation or transfer authorization policies or adding new user roles.

- Any module that hardcoded "EUR" or 10_000m instead of injecting BankSettings would create accounts in the wrong currency or allow transfers above the 5,000 EUR regulatory cap, causing a compliance breach.
- Existing automated tests or downstream integrations that assert "EUR" as the default account currency or 10,000 as the transfer limit will break unless aligned with BankSettings.
